title: How to find your four
sub: Run this on last week and you come out with a short list that is yours, written down, and reusable by anyone else who does your job.

items.title: Start from your own week, not a list of use cases
items.body: Open last week's calendar and sent items. Nothing else.
items.action: List every task over twenty minutes that produced a document or a decision.

items.title: Cross off anything with no file behind it
items.body: If the input only existed in your head, it is not ready to hand over yet.
items.action: Keep only the rows where you could name the file you would attach.

items.title: Circle what you did more than once
items.body: Frequency beats difficulty. A ten-minute job you do daily is worth more than an afternoon you spend twice a year.

items.title: Write each one as a prompt, once
items.body: Name the reader, say what to do with gaps, say what to attach. Three lines, not three paragraphs.
items.action: Keep them in one note, titled by the job rather than by the tool.

items.title: Delete the ones you never opened
items.body: Review the note in a month. The list should get shorter and better, not longer.
items.action: Only add a fifth when it beats one already on the list.
